lsastrat — project overview (orientation & verification guide)

Source: OVERVIEW.md

Purpose of this file: let a new person or LLM understand what this project is, where everything lives, and how to verify it independently. It is not shipped with the package (build-ignored).

What it is

lsastrat is an R package (author: Kevin Schoenholzer, ORCID 0000-0001-9892-5869; IICP, USI Lugano) that computes educational stratification and inequality quantities from large-scale assessment (LSA) data — PISA, TIMSS, PIRLS — as first-class outputs, with statistically correct plausible-value pooling (Rubin’s rules, t reference) and replicate-weight variance (BRR/Fay, JK2, JK1).

The gap it fills: general LSA packages (intsvy, EdSurvey, BIFIEsurvey, Rrepest) pool PVs/weights but only for generic estimators (means, regressions); the stratification quantities, their pooling, and finite-sample bias correction must be hand-assembled. lsastrat packages them.

  • Version: 0.3.0 · Tests: 151 (+1 CI-only parallel) passing · R CMD check --as-cran: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 NOTE (“new submission”).
  • Status: JOSS- and CRAN-ready. JOSS paper drafted (paper/).

Location

  • This package (its own git repo): /Users/kevinschoenholzer/Documents/GitHub/shiny-apps/lsastrat/ → GitHub: https://github.com/kevisc/lsastrat (public) · pkgdown site: https://kevinschoenholzer.com/lsastrat/
  • It is a standalone repo nested inside the (never-pushed) shiny-apps monorepo; commits/pushes happen from the lsastrat/ folder via GitHub Desktop.
  • Real PISA 2022 microdata (for validation only, NOT redistributable per OECD terms) lives outside the package at /Users/kevinschoenholzer/Documents/GitHub/shiny-apps/data/raw/pisa2022/.

What it does (17 exported functions)

Estimators — each returns an lsastrat_estimate object: - social_gradient() — SES (ESCS) → achievement gradient: slope, strength (R²×100), curvature. - segregation_index() — D, Gorard’s S, isolation, Hutchens, Theil’s H, mutual information M; social or PV-pooled academic grouping; replicate or two-stage clustered-bootstrap variance with finite-sample bias correction. - ieop() — Ferreira–Gignoux inequality of educational opportunity (variance share explained by circumstances; raw + df-adjusted). - variance_decomposition() — between/within-school variance and ICC.

Decompositions: ieop_decompose() (Shapley attribution of IOp to each circumstance), oaxaca_gap() (twofold/threefold achievement-gap decomposition).

Comparison & robustness: lsa_by() (run any estimator across countries/subgroups), equity_scatter() (OECD quality-vs-equity plot), lsa_multiverse() + lsa_design() (PV/weight-aware specification curve).

General engine: lsa_model() (fit any lm/glm/multilevel model to PV outcomes with replicate-weight inference).

Shared variance engine (exported for reuse): pool_pv() (Rubin pooling), rep_factor() (BRR/JK multipliers). tidyverse: tidy(), glance().

How to verify (from the lsastrat/ directory)

# 1. install + run the test suite (expect ~151 passing, 0 failures)
devtools::install(); devtools::test()

# 2. full package check (expect 0 errors / 0 warnings; 1 "new submission" NOTE)
devtools::check()        # or: R CMD check --as-cran lsastrat_0.3.0.tar.gz

# 3. quick smoke test
library(lsastrat); data(pisa_mini)
des <- lsa_design(weight = "W_FSTUWT", repweights = paste0("W_FSTURWT", 1:64))
social_gradient(pisa_mini, paste0("PV", 1:10, "MATH"), "ESCS", design = des)

Real-data validation (strongest trust check) — requires the OECD PISA 2022 student file CY08MSP_STU_QQQ.SAV placed where the script expects:

Rscript data-raw/validate_pisa2022.R

It reproduces, for 6 countries, exact agreement (<0.01) of gradient slope/SE/strength with intsvy::pisa.reg.pv and of Theil’s H with the segregation package, and recovers the known between-school-variance contrast (Finland ≈0.12 vs Germany ≈0.47).

How to trust it (what’s already established)

  • Cross-validated against established tools on identical data: social_gradient = intsvy::pisa.reg.pv; segregation D & H = segregation package; ieop = weighted-regression R². (Tests + the PISA-2022 script.)
  • Methodologically reviewed: a multi-lens audit caught and fixed a crash, switched normal→Rubin-t inference, added the segregation bias correction, and the df-adjusted IOp; an adversarial QA pass found no surviving defects.
  • Key design choices: one shared variance engine (pool_pv); inference uses a t reference with Rubin df; segregation bias is removed by a two-stage clustered bootstrap nested inside the PV pooling (a replicate- weight loop structurally cannot do this); optional parallelism via options(lsastrat.cores = n) gives identical results.
